transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-17 16:00 UTC | Duration 47 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Redwood CSM), Daniel Kim (Tellura - Procurement), Aisha Rahman (Tellura - CISO), Evan Stone (Tellura - Platform), Marta Lopez (Tellura - Legal)

Auto-generated summary: Quick procurement intake to nail down DPA/MSA redline path, pricing approval owner, and security validation plan. Customer wants private data residency assurances and KMS integration; concerned about cost tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated.

Topics: DPA redlines, SOC2 and audit evidence, SSO/KMS, private deployment vs dedicated, pricing pilot and procurement timeline, escalation path for security questions.

00:00 Marcus: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um i'll do a quick intro. i'm marcus from redwood, ae on the account. priya our se is here to talk technical, olivia will handle onboarding and pricing. can you quickly intro on your side?
00:18 Daniel: yeah sure this is daniel, head of procurement at tellura. we're kicking off vendor intake for an llm inference partner, timeline is end of q1 go-live ideally.
00:27 Aisha: hi i'm aisha, ciso, i'll be owning security signoff. main things for us are dpa, kms support, sso/saml, and evidence for soc2 plus any fedramp notes if you have them.
00:40 Evan: evan, platform eng - i'll own the pilot execution and performance validation. we'll send sample prompts and baseline p50/p95 latency targets.
00:50 Marcus: great, thanks. quick high level: redwood supports hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private vpc/on-prem. most enterprise flows here are either dedicated or private for pii regulated workloads. for pricing we typically propose a short pilot with committed dedicated capacity and a conversion path.
01:05 Priya: yeah hi all, just to add: from technical lens, we'll need to understand seq lengths, typical batch sizes, and whether you need kv cache retention across sessions. also any transformer model family preferences, and whether you care about 8-bit quantization or better fp16 across the fleet.
01:20 Marta: legal side, i want to understand the dpa exceptions process. last vendor we onboarded took 8 weeks on dpa redlines. what's your typical cadence?
01:32 Marcus: fair question. standard cadence is 1-2 weeks for our initial DPA + MSA template; once redlines come in we triage with legal and can escalate to commercial. if there are high-risk clauses (data residency, audit right limits) that will take longer. we do have an executive escalation path if a customer needs exceptions faster.
01:48 Aisha: can you confirm where customer data is logged? retention windows? we need KMS support and so encryption at rest with our own keys is preferred.
01:58 Priya: yes, we support KMS integration on private deployments and Dedicated has support for BYOK depending on the commit tier. for hosted the default is redwood-managed keys but there are enterprise options. logging - audit logs are available, we can configure retention windows as part of the console.
02:14 Daniel: so from procurement the pricing question is important - if we go dedicated what is the minimum commit and how flexible are burst policies? our usage is spiky tied to some monthly batch jobs.
02:26 Marcus: dedicated reserves a GPU pool, minimum varies by region and sku; we typically provide a flexible burst bucket for transient spikes. i'll send a pricing tier matrix after this call. pilot discounts are common.
02:35 Evan: for perf validation, can you simulate our longest context runs? we have some 8k tokens cases for summarization.
02:44 Priya: yes, we can. we usually suggest a focused perf run: sample job with your prompts, measure p50/p95, token cost, and memory headroom. for >4k contexts we might recommend specific kernel optimizations and maybe quantization tradeoffs - we'll show that in the run.
02:58 Marta: any concerns about regulatory cross-border data flows? some of our data must stay in eu-resident infrastructure.
03:06 Marcus: we have private deployments in eu regions and on-prem packages, plus the dedicated capacity can be pinned to region. i'll note that in the follow-up.
03:14 Aisha: ok, we'll need SOC2 report and pen-test summary. do you provide attestation or just summarize?
03:21 Olivia: we provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA and a pen-test executive summary; for more detailed evidence we have an audit intake process. i'll share links in the follow-up.
03:34 Daniel: procurement needs a clean path to pricing approval. who signs off on the pilot terms?
03:39 Marcus: typically procurement signs the pilot SOW and finance signs the billing terms; commercial can route to an approval path per your contract matrix.
03:46 Evan: any notes about routing/fallback? if the dedicated pool is saturated do requests fail or route to hosted?
03:53 Priya: we support routing policies: you can choose strict isolation (fail-over disabled) or automatic fallback to a compatible variant in hosted tier. that does have cost and data residency implications.
04:07 Daniel: let's talk about timeline - procurement would like to lock pilot terms by 12/24 to fit internal cycles. is that realistic?
04:13 Marcus: yes that's tight but doable if legal redlines and security artifacts are small. main risk is if legal asks for non-standard DPA clauses; that pushes timeline. we should aim to get your redline back asap.
04:26 Marta: i'll circulate our redlines by monday 12/21. expected turn around time from your side?
04:33 Marcus: we'll review and respond within 48 hours and escalate any high-priority exceptions.
04:39 Aisha: what about SSO and role mapping? we use SAML with SCIM provisioning, and need fine-grained RBAC for route-level access.
04:49 Priya: supported. we have SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning, and RBAC is configurable in the console per route/model. for private deployments we can add extra enforcement hooks. note: some older transcript here - scim provisioning name sometimes gets mis- transcribed in notes.
05:04 Evan: ok, point on billing: we need token-level metering exported to our billing system and daily usage breakdowns.
05:12 Olivia: we can export usage via S3 or push to APIs, and set retention for raw logs. cost attribution per token and per model is a built-in dashboard.
05:21 Daniel: competitor question - last week some stakeholders asked about going to anth... anthropic or vertex - what are your differentiation points?
05:30 Marcus: short answer: production economics and control. we give tooling for batching/caching, dedicated routing, and an ops surface for rollouts. also we try to be transparent about per-token unit cost and tradeoffs for latency.
05:43 Aisha: any fedramp or healthcare specific compliance? we're in healthcare so a lot of PHI controls matter.
05:51 Priya: not fedramp certified today; we have customers in healthcare under private deployments with contractual controls and audits. for PHI we recommend private deployment or dedicated with strict retention settings and BYOK.
06:04 Marta: legal nit - indemnity and liability caps. we may need higher cap for PHI exposure, how flexible is that?
06:13 Marcus: that's typically negotiated at enterprise tier; we can discuss an elevated cap in commercial terms but it requires procurement/legal approval and may affect pricing.
06:24 Evan: technical - can you preserve kv cache between sessions for performance? some of our agents rely on warm cache across calls.
06:33 Priya: yes, persistent kv cache is supported on dedicated and private modes; hosted api has ephemeral caches. depending on memory footprint we'll size the cluster.
06:44 Daniel: okay, next what do we need to move forward? for procurement: redline, pricing, pilot sod - sorry s o w.
06:53 Marcus: yes s o w, pilot scope. action plan: customer to send redlines and sample prompts/dataset; redwood will run perf test and return results plus a pricing SOW; legal and security artifacts will be shared in follow-up.
07:06 Marta: one more legal process question - we have a standard clause requiring 30-day data deletion after termination, is that compatible?
07:14 Priya: yes we support configurable retention windows and data deletion workflows; for private deployments we can guarantee data purge procedures with attestation.
07:25 Aisha: about kms - how is key rotation handled if we bring our own key?
07:31 Marcus: BYOK supports rotation but we need coordination windows for re-keying. our ops runbooks outline rotation steps and secrets bootstrap. we'll include that doc.
07:44 Evan: any gotchas with network egress and firewall rules for private vpc?
07:50 Priya: we usually provide a network diagram and required firewall ports, and we can do an onboarding network runbook with your infra team.
07:59 Daniel: ok this is helpful. procurement follow up would like a clear decision path for pilot pricing - who will own that on your side?
08:07 Olivia: i'll own the pilot pricing and draft the SOW, i'll send a first pass by 2026-12-20.
08:13 Marcus: i'll send DPA redline and SOC2 pointer by 12/18 and coordinate any contract exceptions with legal.
08:19 Priya: i'll schedule the perf run once evan shares sample prompts; target completion 12/24.
08:25 Marta: we'll aim to return redlines by 12/21 and confirm procurement approver.
08:31 Aisha: last question - is there a standard SLA for p50/p95?
08:36 Priya: we publish model performance profiles per model and region; SLAs vary by commitment level. dedicated has SLA-backed latency 99% uptime commitments; specifics will be in the SOW.
08:48 Daniel: if we do a pilot and like the results what's the conversion cadence to full contract?
08:55 Marcus: typical path is pilot -> committed capacity negotiation -> 30/60/90 day ramp. we'll propose conversion terms in the pilot SOW.
09:05 (brief cross talk)
09:12 Marcus: ok, let's do a quick recap and actions. olivia?
09:16 Olivia: recap: redwood to provide DPA + SOC2 summary (Marcus), pilot SOW and pricing (Olivia) by 12/20, se perf run (Priya) after sample prompts, customer to return redlines by 12/21.
09:32 Daniel: that works, we'll see if exec approver is available that week.
09:36 Marcus: excellent. any other open items?
09:40 Aisha: no, just please include pen-test summary and the audit intake flow in the follow up.
09:46 Olivia: will do.
09:48 Marcus: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and slack.
09:52 Meeting end.
